messages:
liz: Heads-up — ran into a nasty tail-latency spike during a simulated eu->us failover this morning. Seems cold KV cache + model cold-starts are additive.

mike: ugh. can you paste the load profile? was it bursty or steady ramp?

liz: short burst (5k reqs over 30s) for a single tenant we shipped to eu1. p50 fine, p95 jumped to ~2.1s, p99 ~4.8s. linked the perf dashboard: https://dash.redwood.internal/r/xyz (infra-bot posted snap) :grimacing:

infra-bot: snapshot: region=eu1->us1 failover sim, metrics: p50=120ms p95=2.1s p99=4.8s, kv-miss-rate=78%, model-loads=23, concurrent-spins=6

sarah: important: that tenant opted into EU residency. any prewarming or replication needs to keep data in-eu or we violate contract. are we sure the failover path is allowed to pull cached PII over the wire?

dan: good call. current fallback policy routes to nearest available region and will stream hooks to model instances there. we treat KV cache as ephemeral derived state; but some cache entries include tenant-scoped keys that reference userid or email. we need to differentiate PII vs opaque cache handles.

bryan: quick idea: separate cache namespaces. residency=true tenants only get "eu-resident" namespace that is never replicated outside eu. fallback to non-resident region only allowed if we can recreate cache without PII (i.e., rebuild from master with hash-only keys).

mike: +1 to namespace split. implementation quirk: rebuilding cache on failover is slow. we could prewarm model weights and generic prefixes but not tenant-specific data. that should reduce model cold-start + prefix-kv miss somewhat.

liz: so playbook option A = prewarm everything (fast but may move derived PII off-region and expensive). option B = prewarm code+model kernels and only non-PII cache entries. option C = no prewarm, rely on degraded latency but preserve strict residency. which is realistic?

sarah: legal prefers B or C. B if we can certify the cache keys are non-PII and we log QA for each tenant. also need opt-in from enterprise customers for any cross-region derived-state moves.

dan: technically we can mark cache entries with a residency tag at write time. on failover we selectively fetch only entries tagged "replicable". tags are tiny and cheap. downside: tags add an extra read path on hot writes (~1 extra write meta op).

bryan: we measured tag overhead ~3% CPU and <1ms p50 on writes — acceptable. the bigger cost is bandwidth and storage for prewarming if we replicate across regions proactively.

mike: another hybrid: incremental soft-warm. once a tenant shows sustained traffic in standby region for N minutes, we replicate only the top-K most-accessed prefixes (LRU). reduces bandwidth and targets high-hit items.

liz: nice. that aligns with our cost-aware thesis. could we tie this to tenant tier? e.g., enterprise customers get guaranteed warm failover, free-tier gets cold fallback.

sarah: yes but need to reflect in contracts and our SLA page. legal will need a checkbox for cross-region replication.

dan: ops note — for simulated failovers we should add a step to run the following probe to measure cold-path latency:

bryan: ```
# run from failover region host
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.internal/v1/infer?tenant=TENANT_ID\
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN'\
  -d '{"prompt":"warmup-probe"}' -w '\nHTTP: %{http_code} T=%{time_total}s\n'
```

mike: also we should instrument a warmup score for a tenant (hotness metric). if hotness > threshold, autoscaler should trigger async replication of top-K prefixes.

liz: actionables I propose: 1) implement residency-tagging on cache writes (dan), 2) design soft-warm algorithm (mike + bryan), 3) update failover runbook with probe and legal checklist (liz + sarah), 4) add tenant opt-in flag in billing/console for cross-region prewarm (product), 5) simulate 5 failure runs and capture perf.

sarah: adding requirement: any replication must be auditable and reversible. keep KMS logs for the transfer handshake.

dan: noted. tech note: we'll need an idempotent reconciliation job to scrub replicated derived-state when returning to primary. otherwise cache drift and billing confusion.

bryan: mock implementation sketch for tagging payload (for review):
```json
{
  "key": "tenant:1234:prefix:abc",
  "value": "...",
  "residency_tag": "eu-resident" // or "replicable"
}
```

liz: perfect. last thought — add a canary toggle so we can test B on 5 tenants first. reduce blast radius.

mike: +1. i'll start a small spike this afternoon.

infra-bot: Created issue: INFRA-1428 "residency-tagged-cache + soft-warm playbook" assigned to dan/mike/liz. Link: https://issues.redwood/internal/INFRA-1428

liz: thanks. let's sync in tomorrow's arch sync and aim to have a short RFC for the playbook by EOD Friday. :thumbsup:
